paper.title: Parallel Online Clustering of Bandits via Hedonic Game

settings.name_in_paper: Online clustering of bandits (parallel, n users in m clusters, linear stochastic payoffs)
unmapped: n users act in parallel each round; users in the same (unknown) cluster share the same parameter theta; regret summed over all users
each user's action set of L contexts is drawn i.i.d. each round from a random vector X with ||X||<=1 and E[XX^T] of minimal eigenvalue lambda_min > 0 (Assumption 2)
well-separatedness: distinct cluster parameters differ by at least gamma (Assumption 1)
the learner is assumed to know a lower bound on lambda_min
settings.definition_quote: a_{i,t}(x) = θ_i^T x + ϵ_{i,t}, where θ_i is a fixed but unknown feature vector of agent i and ϵ_{i,t} is a conditionally zero-mean, sub-Gaussian noise with variance parameter σ^2(x) ≤ σ^2 ... Assumption 1 (Well-separatedness) ... ∥θ_j − θ_j'∥ ≥ γ > 0. Assumption 2 (Action regularity) ... D_{i,t} generated i.i.d. from a random vector X, ∥X∥ ≤ 1, such that E[XX^T] is full rank with minimal eigenvalue λ_min > 0.

bound.regime: T > max{128/(3 delta lambda_min) log(128/(3 delta lambda_min)) + 3, 512/(gamma^2 lambda_min)(d lambda_min gamma^2/512 + 1 + 2 log(2/delta) + sigma^2 d log(512 sigma^2/(lambda_min gamma^2))), 4 Omega^2 log(T+1)/gamma^2}

symbols.lambda_min: minimal eigenvalue of E[XX^T] for the context distribution
symbols.gamma_sep: separation gap between distinct cluster parameter vectors

conditions: Assumption 1: distinct cluster vectors separated by gamma > 0
Assumption 2: contexts i.i.d. with ||X||<=1 and lambda_min(E[XX^T]) > 0

source.quote: Let the CLUB-HG algorithm described in Algorithm 1 runs with a set of agents V = {1, 2, . . . , n}, which can be partitioned into m clusters ... Let Assumption 1 and 2 hold. ... Then with probability at least 1 − δ, the cumulative regret satisfies R(T) ≤ Õ(n/(λ_min γ^2) + √(dmnT)(σ√d + 1)), as T grows large (more precisely, for T > max{...}). Because of Õ notation, the factors log(1/δ), log(d), and log(T) do not appear.

results.notes: Õ hides log(1/delta), log d, log T. The explicit form in the proof is A n tau + 3 sqrt(mnT 2d log(1+nT/d))(sigma sqrt(d log(1+nT/d)+2log(1/delta))+1), where A bounds the payoff. Horizon marked anytime because the tuning does not use T. A distributed variant (Algorithm 3) is claimed to have the same bound.

bound.regime: T <= max{128/(3 delta lambda_min) log(128/(3 delta lambda_min)) + 3, 512/(gamma^2 lambda_min)(d lambda_min gamma^2/512 + 1 + 2 log(2/delta) + sigma^2 d log(512 sigma^2/(lambda_min gamma^2))), 4 Omega^2 log(T+1)/gamma^2}

conditions: Assumption 1: distinct cluster vectors separated by gamma > 0
Assumption 2: contexts i.i.d. with ||X||<=1 and lambda_min(E[XX^T]) > 0

source.quote: Let the CLUB-HG algorithm described in Algorithm 1 run with a set of agents V = {1, 2, . . . , n}, which can be partitioned into m clusters ... Assume that Assumption 1 and 2 hold. ... When the sampling steps is not large enough such that T ≤ max{...}, with probability at least 1 − δ the cumulative regret satisfies R(T) ≤ Õ(n√(dT)(σ√d + 1)).

results.notes: Short-horizon regime. The proof also contains a term 4 Omega n sqrt(T log T), which is absorbed into the Õ notation.
